# Genuine parser-v1 / schema-6 synthetic generations

These text JSON fixtures contain exact SQL row values emitted by the unmodified PR40 parser-v1 adapter and durable SQLite writer. They are not relabeled parser-v2 checkpoints and are never re-signed by the integration tests.

## Provenance

- Repository: WhiteKiwi/agentprof
- PR40 supplied head: 646f58e0
- Verified PR40 source tree: 55a4d7be76d03b3e077e538d98adbf0f6bb554dc
- Original materialized tree: 214 files matched the publication manifest before generation
- Node: v24.19.0
- Schema 6, parser version 1, normalization/key versions 1, fixed synthetic identity key only
- Raw input: 661 bytes, two synthetic records (Grep call and completed result)
- Linux dump independently equals every row produced by actual PR40 ingestSourceFile at the same fixed synthetic source path
- Darwin dump generated by the same unchanged PR40 adapter/exportCheckpoint/durable-writer APIs using the Darwin physical path identity; macOS filesystem execution is NOT RUN in this Linux environment

The maintenance generator is part of the planning evidence, generate-v1-fixtures.mjs. Regeneration requires the separately provenance-verified PR40 build. The normal integration test requires only these JSON files, current project code and built-in Node modules. No network, historical binary, vendored parser or extra dependency is used at test runtime.

## Why two identities?

Authenticated generations bind the exact source path through HMAC. Changing a fixture's path would require rewriting and re-signing old state, invalidating the historical-generation test. Linux uses /tmp; macOS uses /private/tmp because AgentProf correctly rejects symlinked path components. The existing product supports Linux and macOS only.

Each test process exclusively acquires the fixed synthetic directory with mkdir (no recursive creation), failing if it already exists. It never adopts or deletes another process's directory. Cleanup occurs only after acquisition. Two simultaneous executions of this same test file therefore cause a visible lock failure, not interference or silent skipping. If a process is killed, inspect the clearly named synthetic directory before manually removing it; the test does not reclaim it automatically.

Fresh databases receive the fixture rows verbatim in one transaction. The loader checks the whole-fixture SHA-256, raw-byte SHA-256, exact table and column names, schema version, parser version, revision and checkpoint authentication. Each test uses an independent SQLite data directory. Public readiness flags remain false.

## Scope

The fixture JSON includes only synthetic metadata and safe HMAC state. No actual user logs, paths, credentials, source code or output are included. The synthetic HMAC key is intentionally public test data.
